fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Priest as Mediator", "body": "Chance Garton and Dylan Saccoccio build the whole episode around one idea, that the priest is a mediator standing between heaven and earth. They trace the mediator archetype through Mithra wrestling the bull, described as an Iranian deity of covenant, light, oath and justice, and through Hebrews 8, where Moses is called a mediator using the Greek root MES, which also signifies the midday sun. From there the same root runs into Mesembria, Mesopotamia and Hermes, the savior mediator whose name gives us hermeticism. The pontifex maximus, the great bridge builder, is presented as the surviving office of that role."}, {"title": "Beggars on Horseback", "body": "Dylan opens with the old expression that if you set a beggar on horseback he will ride to the devil, meaning people unaccustomed to wealth or power tend to be corrupted by it. He tells the story of putting out a fire while thirty people ran, and uses the Witcher as his model of a useful outsider society never quite welcomes. Chance links the word person to parson, a beneficed member of the clergy, and to the benefice, which reframes Pope Boniface and the Pope as the beneficiary in a global trust arrangement."}, {"title": "Robert Taylor and the Astronomical Tabernacle", "body": "Much of the free portion works through Reverend Robert Taylor, the clergyman who called communicants theophagists, or God flesh eaters, and mocked the heavenly lamb with hellish sauce. Taylor argues that the blue curtain of the tabernacle with its cherubim was nothing but an orrery, a working picture of the heavens. The priests, in scarlet and gold spangles on a blue ground, personated Mercury, Jupiter, the sun, the moon and the twelve signs. Chance reads the passage aloud, and both hosts treat it as proof that temple ritual was astronomy in costume."}, {"title": "Moses, Moshe, and Mexico", "body": "The hosts argue that Moses is not a single historical man but a recurring solar and initiatory title. Moshe was a term for an initiate in Egypt, and being drawn from the waters encodes baptism and rebirth into a brotherhood, the same pattern found in later secret societies. The same consonants give Messiah and Mashiach. Taylor is quoted noting that the Mexicans, who had never heard of Jew or Christian before Cortez and Pizarro, called the founder of their race Mexi or Messi, with Huitzilopochtli, robed in blue like the ephod, as their Jehovah."}, {"title": "Aita, the Etruscan Father", "body": "Dylan's proudest claim is philological. Aita, spelled A I T A, is the Basque word for father, priest and author, and it appears on an Etruscan tomb centuries older than the oldest Basque inscription, written right to left like Hebrew. Aita is also Hades, god of the underworld, and Chance connects that to the great father attribute of Osiris style deities, which is why priests call themselves fathers. Dylan says nobody addresses this evidence in public debate, which is why he is withdrawing, and Chance offers ultracrepidarian as the older word for the Dunning Kruger effect."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: The role of the priest as mediator appears across ancient religions, mythologies, and esoteric traditions. The Pope is called Pontifex Maximus. Moses mediates between Israel and the divine. Hermes mediates between the gods and mortals.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In Inner Whirled 8, Chance and co-host Dylan Saccoccio explore the symbolism of the priesthood through scripture, etymology, and the astronomical context of the ancient world.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Priests as the Authors of Royal History", "body": "The members' hour opens with Chance reading Robert Taylor's claim that every nation has had its own book of Genesis, a fabulous creation story shaped by priests to lend dignity to their own people. Chance describes a practice in which a conquering king or emperor enlisted the astronomer priests to write a history of his people, reading judicial astrology in reverse out of the scripture of the stars. Every ruler wanted to trace his lineage to the beginning of a world age, and Chance notes that Homer means hostage, a word that also carries the sense of pledge or security."}, {"title": "Faber, Israel, and the Many Faces of Kronos", "body": "Chance brings in George Faber's Origin of Pagan Idolatry, written from a true believer's stance yet full of historical gravy. Faber concedes that Kronos appears as Noah, as Adam, and in a local Phoenician form as Abraham, the patriarch who sacrificed his only son. A passage from Eusebius quoting Porphyry has the Phoenicians calling Kronos Israel, and Faber's footnotes strain to explain it away as a misreading of El. In doing so he admits El is Sanskrit for world, which Chance says confirms his view that God and the world are the same, while Dylan adds the Italian and Spanish articles il and el."}, {"title": "The Pentateuch as a Priestly Curriculum", "body": "Dylan reads Robert Taylor's decoding of the five books of Moses as a manual of priestcraft. Genesis is an imaginary creation, Exodus the stars coming up from below the horizon into the Milky Way, the land flowing with milk and honey, Leviticus the directions for conducting the mysteries, Numbers a book of allegorical arithmetic, and Deuteronomy the second sense in which one thing is said and another intended. Taylor even maps the books onto addition, subtraction, multiplication with all the benefit going to the clergy, division and reduction. His wilderness is the starry night sky, and the children of Israel are the stars themselves."}, {"title": "The Lord as the Leading Constellation", "body": "Chance reads Taylor on the Lord God of Israel as the leading constellation that brings the children of Israel up out of Egypt, the lamb of the new allegory, reflecting the precessional shift from the bull of Taurus to the ram of Aries, with Dylan's note that Baal and bull are the same word. Dylan insists the Hebrew reads Jova rather than Lord, because without the sun no one would reckon the year. He then describes Taylor's priest playing the Lord in a large white wig, with seven candlesticks for the planets and twelve stones for the zodiac, and traces such wigs from Etruscan art to the periwigs of judges."}, {"title": "Fourteen Generations and the 6,000 Year Clock", "body": "Chance works through Matthew 1:17, where the genealogy runs in three sets of fourteen generations, and Godfrey Higgins's reading of it as precessional arithmetic: 42 generations of 71.5 years gives 3003, 56 gives the orthodox 4004, and 84 completes the 6,000 years of the mythos. Dylan explains why seventy stands for seventy two, with the degrees above and below the horizon making 144. The 6,000th year marks the Messianic age in Jewish tradition, followed by a fallow seventh millennium, and Chance lines up Adam, Noah, Abraham, David, Cyrus and Jesus as great father incarnations a thousand years apart."}]

I'm ready to have some fun.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "there's an expression in the old world a couple hundred years ago when it was pertinent that if you set a beggar on horseback, they'll ride to the devil and you see that with fame, fortune, all these things, when people get a lot of influence, they do bad things with it", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "Mithra is wrestling the bull with a sun, which signifies mediator or one who binds a covenant, contract or oath and Wiki, just to quote them, describes Mithra as an ancient Iranian deity of covenant, light, oath, justice, the sun, contracts and friendship.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "it bears repeating over and over again that the Disneyfied version of mythology that we have now with these big pantheons and all of their humanized antics is a pretty far stretch from how the original system was conceived and what it was meant to be", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "And so that saved by the waters, saved from the waters, all that symbolism, it's basically encoding baptism and being born again into a new brotherhood. And in order to keep that astronomy precise, they created the astrology or astro theology to remind them that way you could take it with you", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "the priests dressed themselves up in the imaginary characters of the constellations and planets.
